independence_caveat: Same model family as the other reviewers; agreement is reading consistency, not independent validation.

findings.finding: Topology map: C1 is stated as a corpus inventory of three realized response forms, with the three equations given explicitly. Its operative premises are model-specific entropy functions and the absence of an assumed common sigma_s normalization; the manuscript also withholds identification of dS/d rho, the relativistic source term, and the grid-action Gamma as one normalized physical object. Thus C1 is a fixed-snapshot model-family claim, not a unification claim; reading it as one common physical response would be broader than the text.
findings.test: Compare the three equations with the normalization and non-identification caveats in Section 3; verify that they are corpus realizations rather than one selected normalized physical object.
findings.reasoning: The equations occur at lines 139-147, while the model-specific entropy and normalization premises occur at lines 133-137 and the cross-implementation non-identification constraint occurs at line 149. The claim-set sentence preserves the inventory but omits those limiting premises, so the topology requires the narrower reading.

findings.finding: C2 is a compound topology: it combines the absence of an A-to-B-to-C maturation chain, the shape-bifurcation classification, and the existence of one declared-but-undemonstrated B-to-B+ relation. Its premises are the stated statuses proposed, declared derived, and declared companion upgrade, together with no established supersession or physical selection. The phase is the fixed model-family reconciliation, not an empirical selection.
findings.source_location: snapshot.tex:151-161, Section 3, model-family statuses and structural statement
findings.test: Audit the ledger relation and package statuses, then check whether any discriminating B/B+ selection is recorded; the topology is retained only if the edge remains declared and unselected.
findings.reasoning: Lines 154-156 assign the individual statuses, and lines 161-162 explicitly deny a linear maturation chain while describing the B-to-B+ edge as declared and undemonstrated. These are linked but separable propositions, so the claim is compound and must retain all three status premises.

findings.finding: C3 combines a dimensional diagnosis, a normalization condition, and a source-package provenance statement. It assumes rho and rho_crit remain dimensional densities: Gamma_B then carries sqrt([rho]), whereas Gamma_A and Gamma_C are dimensionless; common normalization is withheld pending a prefactor or reference scale. The text locates this defect in package 31942821 and reports it rather than repairing it. It is a model-construction-phase statement, not a claim that Gamma_B has been rejected.
findings.source_location: snapshot.tex:139-149, Section 3, dimensional qualification of Gamma forms
findings.test: Perform a dimensional audit using the declared units of rho and rho_crit, and inspect package 31942821 for the stated key-result expression and any source-supplied prefactor or reference scale.
findings.reasoning: Line 149 supplies all three topology components: the residual dimension, the restriction on common normalization, and the statement that the inconsistency is present in the source package. Treating this as only a formula claim would drop its provenance and phase qualifiers.

findings.finding: C4 maps to one relation label plus one status field: B-to-B+ is called a declared companion upgrade, while supersession remains not established. The manuscript's premise is that upgrade is ledger vocabulary, not a statement of physical improvement, and that B+ is untested. The claim is therefore a model-family relation in an open-selection phase; interpreting upgrade as empirical improvement would be broader than the text.
findings.source_location: snapshot.tex:154-161, Section 3, Gamma_C status and B-to-B+ relation
findings.test: Read the companion-package and ledger status fields together and check whether a discriminating test or explicit supersession status has been added.
findings.reasoning: The relation label appears at lines 156 and 161, and the text explicitly denies that upgrade implies physical improvement, improved fit, dimensional consistency, or supersession. The claim is topologically faithful only with that status-only interpretation.

findings.finding: C5 combines a two-axis taxonomy with the open status of both axes. The manuscript defines an E-exponent axis and a Gamma-shape axis, says they are separate descriptive axes, and separately warns that physical independence is not demonstrated; it also distinguishes these model-family axes from the proposed test axes. Only the E axis has a current preregistration proposal, while neither axis has an executed selection. Reading separate as physically independent would be broader than the text.
findings.source_location: snapshot.tex:163-186, Section 4 and Table 2, two model-family axes
findings.test: Check the axis definitions and status table against the discriminator section, then verify that no executed test selects either the E-exponent or Gamma-shape axis.
findings.reasoning: Lines 166-172 provide the descriptive separation and its physical-independence caveat; lines 181-186 mark both axes open. The claim-set shorthand needs those premises to avoid collapsing descriptive taxonomy into a physical independence assertion.

findings.finding: C6 is compound: it identifies two mathematical roles for a square root and adds a non-entailment rule. The E-axis exponent acts on g through E proportional to sqrt(g), while the Gamma-axis form uses sqrt(rho/rho_crit); selecting one is not stated to select the other. The manuscript separates the roles and explicitly leaves physical independence undemonstrated, so the claim is a representational distinction rather than a completed physical decoupling.
findings.test: Parse the dependency graph of the E-exponent and Gamma-shape definitions and verify that no equation in the manuscript derives one square-root choice from the other.
findings.reasoning: The two formulas and the explicit non-conflation statement are colocated in lines 168-172. The same passage says the two axes' physical independence is not demonstrated, which is a necessary qualifier missing from any stronger reading of C6.

findings.finding: C7 is an explicit conditional criterion, not an observed result. Its condition is conjunctive: robust, bias-controlled and diverse galaxy data must prefer the linear-g-in-the-exponent form mu(g)=1/(exp(g/a0)-1) and significantly exclude the sqrt(g) form at >=5 sigma; only then does the stated conditional conclusion falsify the E proportional to sqrt(g) theorem. The phase is future external-data testing of the E axis, and the manuscript calls the threshold pre-declared rather than reported.
findings.test: Predeclare the data, bias controls, system diversity, model comparison and 5-sigma rule, then execute the comparison without treating the conditional threshold as an existing result.
findings.reasoning: Line 194 supplies the full antecedent and consequent, while line 198 explicitly states that the threshold is unexecuted or externally referenced and remains open. The topology is preserved only when all antecedent clauses and the conditional status remain attached.

The source layer is package metadata as described by the manuscript, not independent empirical evidence. The phase is provenance reconciliation; the text leaves open whether the exclusion is an executed fit or an external reference.

findings.reasoning: Lines 198 and 241 identify the null fields, no-fit status, unresolved provenance branch, and author gate. C8 is therefore a compound provenance map; it should not be read as a determination of whether the exclusion itself is valid.

findings.finding: C9 is compound: it combines the proposed status of Discriminator 1, its non-execution, the list of circulating a0 candidates, and the requirement that exactly one value be author-frozen and provenance-labelled before the retrodiction. The stated premise is that 1.2e-10 is provisional source-package input rather than an EFC-derived prediction; alternatives include 6.5e-10 and a0_eff=C^2 a0. Its regime/phase is the E-axis SPARC/RAR test before author freeze, not an executed measurement.
findings.test: Freeze exactly one a0 value with its provenance label before fitting, then run the specified SPARC/RAR retrodiction and report it as the predeclared test rather than as a fitted prediction.
findings.reasoning: Lines 217-220 state proposal status, non-execution, all candidate values, the freeze rule, and the distinction between input, output, and nuisance calibration. Omitting any of these turns a status topology into a stronger prediction claim.

findings.finding: C10 is compound: it joins the proposed and unexecuted status of the siren discriminator, the relativistic distance-ratio expression, the unfrozen coupling parameters alpha, phi0 and phi(z), and the condition for EFC-specific discrimination. Its premises include the field-normalization condition [alpha phi]=1 and the separate scope of this test from the Gamma-shape axis. The regime/phase is the future propagation sector, not a present observation; dL^GW != dL^EM alone is explicitly non-specific.
findings.test: Freeze alpha, phi0 and phi(z) numerically with field normalization, define the competing propagation models, and execute the multi-messenger distance comparison.
findings.reasoning: Line 221 provides the expression, dimensional condition, unfrozen parameters, non-specificity caveat, and author-gated freeze step. These are distinct logical layers within C10 and must remain attached to the proposed-test label.

findings.finding: C11 is a three-part scope assertion: no new fit is executed, no selection is made on the named model-family alternatives, and no independent package validation is claimed. The manuscript's named scope includes no B/B+ selection, no E-exponent selection, no Gamma-shape selection, no independent validation, and no physical falsification. These are claims about this reconciliation's phase and evidentiary scope, not a universal statement that no such tests exist anywhere in the corpus.

findings.reasoning: Lines 225-234 enumerate the negative scope statements. Because C11 compresses several independently scoped negatives, its topology is lost if 'no axis selection' is generalized beyond the named B/B+, E-exponent and Gamma-shape alternatives.

findings.finding: C12 contains two independent workflow propositions: byte identity is not currently reproducible because pdfTeX embeds a wall-clock timestamp and per-run trailer identifier unless suppressed, while the current build is reported to complete without Overfull/Underfull hbox or float-placement warnings. The first is a build-system diagnosis and the second is a run-status observation; warning-free output does not establish byte reproducibility. The phase is an open reproducibility workflow item.

findings.reasoning: Line 346 explicitly separates the open byte-for-byte property from the reported warning status. C12 is therefore compound and should not be collapsed into either a general claim of build failure or a claim that warning-free output proves reproducibility.

findings.finding: C13 is a compound regime map with three layers: a candidate single-framework regime ontology, a LambdaCDM global linear/screened L0/L1 special-case declaration, and a MOND-like local low-acceleration IR emergent-response declaration. The manuscript explicitly distinguishes formal-limit declaration from regime interpretation, labels the latter an unproven hypothesis, and says neither row is an equal-footing empirical recovery. The claim-set shorthand is broader if those qualifiers are omitted. The source is the manuscript's Review status prose, treated here as ordinary author text rather than independent evidence.

findings.reasoning: The two rows at lines 281-284 give the formal-limit and emergent-response placements, while lines 294-304 explicitly add the evidence-versus-ontology distinction and the unproven status. The claim therefore touches regime, emergence and epistemic phase, but cannot be mapped as an empirical unification result.
